learning_outcomes.text: Students will acquire basic aspects of a specific future topic and be sensitized to the associated personal or societal challenges.

Students will be enabled to generate insights in inter- and transdisciplinary working groups and relate them to their respective professional background. They will be encouraged to articulate their own disciplinary perspective and explain it to others, as well as to adopt and discuss the perspectives of other disciplines.
Students will acquire transversal competencies that they can apply in their professional life and/or within social engagement.

If students take courses that involve research-related projects, e.g., as part of research-based learning, they will generate research- and project-based insights. Depending on the application context, they will develop their own research questions, apply different research methods, and explain the results of their research.

Depending on the course format, students will communicate and cooperate in interdisciplinary working groups on the specific future topic. They will be able to reflect on and consider different perspectives and interests of other participants.
Students will be able to adequately assess their individual portfolio of future-oriented competencies and use them profitably for their life and career planning.

assessment_rules: Graded examination performances are not foreseen in the interdisciplinary Future Skills module. The selection of the ungraded examination type(s) is the responsibility of the respective lecturer, who adheres to the valid study regulations. A new examination form for the interdisciplinary Future Skills module (SkillsBook) is to be included in the ATPO as soon as possible. When 150 work units are completed and 5 ECTS points are earned, the module will be marked as passed.
